signals.title: NZD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + ESI Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5959, extending its position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster following a 2.061% G10 spread outperformance against the USD. The move is fundamentally anchored by the RBNZ at 2.5% [HIKING] vs a Fed on hold at 3.75%, where a 125bp USD carry advantage is being actively offset by a sharp divergence in economic data momentum. The US Economic Surprise Index (ESI) has fallen to -15.1, reflecting persistent data misses, while the NZD ESI remains positive at +5.1. Speculative positioning in NZD remains crowded at a 52-week percentile of 2 (z-score -2.00), suggesting the current rally is fueled by a high-conviction short-covering cycle. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD; technical breakout supported by short-unwind momentum. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — hike probability elevated. Risk: US data turnaround reverses the ESI divergence and stabilizes USD downside.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Macro Repricing + Technical Cluster
signals.text: USD/JPY is testing 159.07, currently holding below the SMA20 at 159.67 and SMA50 at 161.01. BoJ holds at 1.0%. Options markets are aggressively hedging downside risk, with the 1M 25d risk reversal at -2.02, while the USD/JPY vs VIX correlation (+0.432 vs norm +0.232) confirms JPY is no longer trading on safe-haven flows but on policy repricing. Speculative shorts have begun to cover, with JPY LF net WoW rising by +4,107, yet the net short of -59,526 remains substantial. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; hawkish BoJ pivot overrides the 264bp OIS carry disadvantage. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 63% hike priced) 18 Sep — hike bias dominant. Risk: US Treasury yields spike further, reviving the carry-trade bid and stalling the JPY recovery.

signals.title: GBP/USD — COT vs Options Divergence
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3639, supported by a neutral 11bp carry advantage (SONIA 3.73% vs SOFR 3.62%). Speculative positioning is approaching crowded territory with LF net long at +42,722 (90th percentile, z+1.23) after four weeks of sustained adds totaling +14,444. However, the options market is signaling caution; despite the price rally, the 25d risk reversal remains flat at +0.05 while ATM IV (11.0%) commands a massive 5.1-point premium over realized vol (5.9%). This suggests institutional players are paying heavily for protection rather than chasing the long-GBP trend, creating an asymmetric risk profile. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; extreme vol risk premium suggests upside exhaustion. Catalyst: BoE meeting 17 Sep — hold expected. Risk: A clean break above recent highs triggers a final retail capitulation, as retail remains 85% short.

signals.title: USD/CHF — Volatility Complacency + Carry Dominance
signals.text: USD/CHF at 0.8002 remains anchored by the widest carry differential in the G10 space, with a 375bp USD advantage over the SNB at 0.0%. Technical positioning shows the pair holding just above the SMA200 at 0.7930 despite a 1.57% decline over the past week. Options pricing reflects unusual complacency, with 1M IV at 7.2% trailing realized volatility of 8.4% (VRP -1.2%), suggesting the market is underpricing potential mean-reversion in volatility. Speculative positioning is at a 52-week extreme short in CHF (pctl 4, z -2.08), which typically supports USD/CHF upside, though retail sentiment is already 80% long. Trade bias: Long USD/CHF; carry advantage persists while VIX remains in 'normal' regime at 16.0. Catalyst: next SNB meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) 24 Sep. Risk: VIX breaks above 25, triggering a rapid safe-haven CHF bid that compresses the carry spread.
